title: Texas's 11th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 11th Congressional District pits three-term Republican incumbent August Pfluger against Democratic nominee Claire Reynolds and independent candidate Sean Benson. The district, which covers much of West Texas including Midland, Odessa, San Angelo, and parts of the Austin suburbs, is rated as Solidly Republican by the Cook Political Report with a PVI of R+17. Pfluger, a retired U.S. Air Force Colonel and chair of the Republican Study Committee, is seeking a fourth term and faced no primary opposition. Reynolds, an attorney and former prosecutor with the State Bar of Texas, won a contested Democratic primary against Pedro Ruiz in March 2026. The race occurs in a district with a nearly 10-to-1 Republican voter registration advantage, making it one of the most conservative congressional districts in the country.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-2026. The district is considered safely Republican, and major polling firms have not polled the race.

candidates.name: August Pfluger
candidates.summary: August Pfluger is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 11th Congressional District, first elected in 2020 and seeking his fourth term. A retired U.S. Air Force Colonel and F-22 fighter pilot who served over 25 years on active duty and in the reserves, Pfluger chairs the Republican Study Committee and serves on the House Energy and Commerce and Homeland Security Committees. He is a seventh-generation Texan who grew up in San Angelo and has emphasized energy production, national security, and constituent services during his tenure.

career_history.description: F-22 and F-15 fighter pilot; commanded the 380th Expeditionary Operations Group in the Middle East; served on the National Security Council in 2019; retired from active duty in February 2026 after 26 years of service.

candidates.name: Claire Reynolds
candidates.summary: Claire Reynolds is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 11th Congressional District, having won the March 3, 2026 primary with 57.6% of the vote against Pedro Ruiz. She is an attorney who spent 12 years at the State Bar of Texas prosecuting attorney misconduct in the Chief Disciplinary Counsel's Office. Reynolds is a former journalist who earned her journalism degree from Northwestern University's Medill School of Journalism and her J.D. from the University of San Diego School of Law. She moved to Texas in 2007, lives in Austin, and is running on a progressive platform focused on affordability, healthcare, immigration reform, and holding the executive branch accountable.

forecast.rationale: No public polling is available for this race, so confidence is limited (medium) and the forecast relies on structural indicators rather than direct voter measurement. Those indicators overwhelmingly favor the Republican incumbent: August Pfluger is a three-term incumbent running unopposed in the primary in Texas's 11th Congressional District, which is rated Solidly Republican by Cook Political Report with a PVI of R+17 and a nearly 10-to-1 Republican voter registration advantage. The Democratic nominee, Claire Reynolds, won a contested primary (57.6%) but faces extremely unfavorable partisan terrain; independent Sean Benson has minimal public information and organizational strength. Given the district's deep Republican baseline, strong incumbency advantage, and absence of any countervailing indicators, Republicans hold an overwhelming advantage and the seat is Safe Republican.
